What would a pay change do to your take-home?

Compare your salary above with a raise, promotion or job offer. Higher-rate tax, National Insurance and student loan all change how much you keep.

+£10,000 gross+£545 / month net

Moving from £45,000 to £55,000 changes your take-home by +£6,538 a year (+£545 a month). You keep 65% of the extra gross pay; the rest goes in Income Tax and National Insurance. Your next pound at the new salary is taxed at a combined 42%.

Frequently asked questions

How do I work out my salary after tax?

Subtract your Personal Allowance (£12,570), apply 20% to the next £37,700, 40% above that, then take off National Insurance. On £45,000 that leaves £35,920.

What is the difference between gross and net salary?

Gross salary is your pay before any deductions. Net salary is what you keep after Income Tax, National Insurance and any pension or student loan deductions.

Why do I keep a lower share on a higher salary?

Because each higher tax band applies only to the pay above its threshold, your effective rate rises gradually. The table above shows the share you keep at each level.

Are these figures for the whole UK?

They use England, Wales and Northern Ireland rates. Choose Scotland in the calculator for Scottish Income Tax.
